text: Lesson 15 found duplicate rows sharing one event_id in a table that already ran a dedup step. This lesson reads the real code to find out exactly why.
The Glue job deduped on installation_id plus reading_timestamp -- a reasonable-looking key that wasn't actually guaranteed unique.
A Kinesis and Lambda retry wrote the same event twice to raw S3. The resend's timestamp came back re-serialized a few hundred milliseconds off, so the composite key saw two rows instead of one.
The fix dedupes on event_id itself -- generated once at the source and never re-derived on a retry. August is backfilled, and the corrected total matches the installation's own history.
A new test reproduces this exact timestamp-jitter scenario and now runs on every pull request, so it can't silently come back.
